newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF official praises new Romanian government.
newsitem.headline: IMF official praises new Romanian government.

text.p: A senior International Monetary Fund (IMF) official said on Wednesday he believed Romania's new government was committed to reforms which would open the door to fresh Western credits for the Balkan country.

"I have been very pleased by the new government's emphasis on reform," Poul Thomsen, IMF chief negotiator for Romania, told reporters after meeting Petre Roman, chairman of the Senate and number two in the state hierarchy.
"There is no disagreement that the acceleration of the reforms is long overdue, much-needed and will be a key to the success also of the stabilisation programme."
Parliament was debating the government's economic programme on Wednesday and was expected to approve it.
The IMF suspended a three-year standby credit of $460 million this year after criticising the policies of the leftist government thrown out in last month's general election.
Thomsen, in Romania since last week, is establishing initial contacts with the administration. He says formal talks on a new standby arrangement could start in the New Year.
Thomsen said he was pursuing his analysis of Romania's economy. Inflation, he said, would probably be 45 to 50 percent this year, in excess of the 20 percent sought by the IMF.
"I think the underlying rate of inflation is probably higher because there have been delays in increasing some administrative prices," Thomsen said.
Free-spending policies in an election year pushed the budget deficit to about five percent of gross domestic product against initial proposals of 2.2 percent, Roman told reporters.
The programme presented by Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea pledges to tackle economic imbalances, push forward reforms and resume talks with international lenders.
Thomsen said the government would be cautious about taking new initiatives. "Any measures that will increase spending should be considered carefully in the context of a comprehensive programme."
IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus is due to visit Romania next week. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest newsroom, +401 301-0264
